title: Live Polling & Quizzes
description: Real-time interactive polls and quizzes to gauge student understanding and gather instant feedback

teacher.overview: Create and launch polls to check student understanding in real-time. Polls can be multiple choice, true/false, or open-ended.

create: During an active session, click 'Create Poll' button
Choose poll type (Multiple Choice, True/False, Rating, Open-ended)
Set correct answer if it's a quiz
launch: Click 'Launch Poll' to send it to students
Poll appears on all students' screens instantly
manage: Close poll manually or let timer expire
Download results as CSV or PDF
Share results with students if desired

pollTypes.description: Students select one or multiple answers from options
pollTypes.bestFor: Knowledge checks, concept understanding, quick assessments
pollTypes.example: Which of these are programming languages? (A) Python (B) HTML (C) Java (D) CSS
pollTypes.tips: Use 4-5 options, include one 'All of the above' or 'None of the above' when relevant

pollTypes.bestFor: Quick comprehension checks, fact verification, warm-up questions
pollTypes.example: True or False: Photosynthesis occurs in mitochondria
pollTypes.tips: Best for clear, unambiguous statements. Avoid tricky wording

pollTypes.description: Students rate on a scale (1-5 or 1-10)
pollTypes.bestFor: Gauging confidence levels, understanding depth, opinions
pollTypes.example: How confident are you with today's topic? (1=Not at all, 5=Very confident)
pollTypes.tips: Use consistent scales throughout session, explain what each number means

pollTypes.bestFor: Gathering opinions, explanations, creative answers, feedback
pollTypes.example: In one sentence, explain what you learned today
pollTypes.tips: Keep questions focused, review responses after session for insights

tips: Use polls every 10-15 minutes to maintain engagement
Mix different poll types for variety
Set appropriate time limits (30-60 seconds for MCQ, 2-3 minutes for open-ended)
Review results before moving to next topic
Use results to adapt your teaching in real-time
Don't reveal correct answers during session to prevent cheating
canDo: See real-time student responses as they submit
Mark correct answers for quiz mode
cannotDo: Edit poll after launching (must delete and recreate)
See who answered what in anonymous mode
Restart a closed poll in same session
bestPractices: Prepare polls before session for smooth flow
Use polls to identify knowledge gaps
Review results to see if reteaching is needed
Use quiz mode for assessments, regular polls for engagement

student.overview: Participate in live polls during sessions to demonstrate your understanding and engage with the class.

participate: Poll appears automatically on your screen when teacher launches it
Select your answer or type response
Wait for next poll or continue with session
viewResults: Some teachers show results after everyone submits
Check your response history in session details
Review your answers after session ends

tips: Answer honestly to help teacher understand class progress
Don't wait too long - polls may have time limits
Read all options before selecting (for multiple choice)
Pay attention to 'select all that apply' vs 'select one'
If confused, ask question in Q&A instead of guessing
canDo: See your response history after session
Submit within time limit if set
cannotDo: See other students' answers before submitting
See correct answers during session (teacher decides when to reveal)

commonIssues.solution: Refresh page, check internet connection, ensure you're in the correct session, verify session is still active
Check if you selected an option, verify poll is still open, ensure you didn't already submit, try refreshing page
Unfortunately cannot change after submission. Be careful next time. Teacher can see genuine mistakes in analytics

commonIssues.problem: Time ran out before I could answer
commonIssues.solution: Read questions faster next time, ask teacher to extend time limits if consistently too short

participationTips: Answer every poll - it helps you and your teacher
Don't copy answers from classmates - defeats the purpose
Use open-ended polls to share your thoughts
If you don't know the answer, it's okay - polls are for learning
